description_full: Obsidian Energy Ltd. engages in the exploration, development, and production of oil and natural gas in Western Canada. Its portfolio of properties includes unitized and non-unitized light oil, heavy oil, and natural gas production. The company was formerly known as Penn West Petroleum Ltd. and changed its name to Obsidian Energy Ltd. in June 2017. Obsidian Energy Ltd. is headquartered in Calgary, Canada.

financial_summary: Obsidian Energy Ltd. is a small-cap energy business with a $645M market cap on $404M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -12% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are expanding by +4.1pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.
The company is burning through $42M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
Accruals are elevated at -11.0% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.0× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 2.1× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 6.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 12% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
